{{Short description|Part of measure theory mathematics}}
{{more citations needed|date=July 2023}}

'''Carathéodory's criterion''' is a result in [[measure theory]] that was formulated by Greek [[mathematician]] [[Constantin Carathéodory]] that characterizes when a set is [[Lebesgue measurable]].

==Statement==

'''Carathéodory's criterion''': 
Let <math>\lambda^* : {\mathcal P}(\R^n) \to [0, \infty]</math> denote the [[Lebesgue measure|Lebesgue]] [[outer measure]] on <math>\R^n,</math> where <math>{\mathcal P}(\R^n)</math> denotes the [[power set]] of <math>\R^n,</math> and let <math>M \subseteq \R^n.</math>  Then <math>M</math> is [[Lebesgue measurable]] if and only if <math>\lambda^*(S) = \lambda^*(S \cap M) + \lambda^*\left(S \cap M^c\right)</math> for every <math>S \subseteq \R^n,</math> where <math>M^c</math> denotes the [[Complement (set theory)|complement]] of <math>M.</math>
Notice that <math>S</math> is not required to be a measurable set.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Pugh |first=Charles C. |title=Real Mathematical Analysis |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-17770-0 |edition=2nd |pages=388 |language=en}}</ref>

==Generalization==

The Carathéodory criterion is of considerable importance because, in contrast to Lebesgue's original formulation of measurability, which relies on certain topological properties of <math>\R,</math> this criterion readily generalizes to a characterization of measurability in abstract spaces.  Indeed, in the generalization to abstract measures, this theorem is sometimes extended to a ''definition'' of measurability.<ref name=":0" />  Thus, we have the following definition: 
If <math>\mu^* : {\mathcal P}(\Omega) \to [0, \infty]</math> is an [[outer measure]] on a set <math>\Omega,</math> where <math>{\mathcal P}(\Omega)</math> denotes the [[power set]] of <math>\Omega,</math> then a subset <math>M \subseteq \Omega</math> is called '''{{em|<math>\mu^*</math>–measurable}}''' or '''{{em|Carathéodory-measurable}}''' if for every <math>S \subseteq \Omega,</math> the equality<math display=block>\mu^*(S) = \mu^*(S \cap M) + \mu^*\left(S \cap M^c\right)</math>holds where <math>M^c := \Omega \setminus M</math> is the [[Complement (set theory)|complement]] of <math>M.</math>

The family of all <math>\mu^*</math>–measurable subsets is a [[σ-algebra]] (so for instance, the complement of a <math>\mu^*</math>–measurable set is <math>\mu^*</math>–measurable, and the same is true of countable intersections and unions of <math>\mu^*</math>–measurable sets) and the [[Restriction (mathematics)|restriction]] of the outer measure <math>\mu^*</math> to this family is a [[Measure (mathematics)|measure]].
